title: Politeness, requests & invitations
goal: Make polite requests, ask favours and permission, offer, invite, accept and refuse gracefully.
intro:
Hindi is rich in politeness, but it doesn't rely on a word like 'please'. Politeness lives in the **verb form** (दीजिए, दीजिएगा), in little softeners like **ज़रा**, and in the respectful आप.

In this unit you'll learn a scale of politeness for requests, and a new verb form — the **subjunctive** — for 'shall I…?', 'let's…', 'may I…?' and wishes.

grammar.title: A ladder of politeness for requests
grammar.body:
From blunt to very polite:

**दो** (तुम) — 'give' — fine with friends and family
**दीजिए** (आप) — 'please give' — the standard polite form
**दे दीजिए** — adding देना after the stem makes it a smooth, 'for me' request; very natural
**दीजिएगा** — the **polite future imperative**: stem + **-इएगा**. Extra courteous, and slightly deferred: 'would you please…'
**क्या आप … देंगे?** / **… दे सकते हैं?** — 'will you / could you…?'

Any of these can be softened further with **ज़रा** 'just', **प्लीज़**, or the formal **कृपया** / **मेहरबानी करके**.

The extra-polite irregular forms: करना → **कीजिएगा**, देना → **दीजिएगा**, लेना → **लीजिएगा**.

Please do give me a call tomorrow.

grammar.title: The subjunctive: shall I…? let's… may you…
grammar.body:
The subjunctive is simply the **future without -गा/-गी/-गे**:

मैं **करूँ** · तू/वह **करे** · तुम **करो** · हम/आप/वे **करें**
(जाना: जाऊँ, जाए, जाओ, जाएँ · होना: होऊँ/हूँ, हो, हो, हों)

It expresses possibility, suggestion or wish rather than fact:

**Offers / shall I?** — मैं चाय बनाऊँ? 'shall I make tea?'
**Asking permission** — मैं अंदर आऊँ? 'may I come in?'
**Let's / shall we?** — चलें? 'shall we go?', चलो, कुछ खाएँ 'come on, let's eat something'
**Very polite/formal instructions** (signs, announcements) — कृपया ध्यान दें 'please pay attention'
**Wishes and blessings** — आप ख़ुश रहें 'may you be happy'
**After 'want' with a different subject** — मैं चाहता हूँ कि **आप आएँ** 'I want you to come'
**After 'maybe'** — शायद वह आए 'he might come'

dialogue.title: Dinner at the Vermas'
dialogue.setting: Kate has been invited to dinner by her colleague's parents, Mr and Mrs Verma.

lines.speaker: Mrs Verma
lines.native: आइए, आइए! आपका स्वागत है। अंदर आइए।
lines.roman: āiye, āiye! āpkā svāgat hai. andar āiye.
lines.en: Come in, come in! Welcome. Please come inside.

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.native: नमस्ते आंटी, नमस्ते अंकल। यह आपके लिए एक छोटा-सा तोहफ़ा।
lines.roman: namaste āṇṭī, namaste aṅkal. yah āpke liye ek chhoṭā-sā tohfā.
lines.en: Hello aunty, hello uncle. A little gift for you.

lines.speaker: Mr Verma
lines.native: अरे, इसकी क्या ज़रूरत थी! बैठिए, आराम से बैठिए।
lines.roman: are, iskī kyā zarūrat thī! baiṭhiye, ārām se baiṭhiye.
lines.en: Oh, there was no need for this! Sit down, make yourself comfortable.

lines.speaker: Mrs Verma
lines.native: आप क्या लेंगी — चाय, या कुछ ठंडा?
lines.roman: āp kyā leṃgī — chāy, yā kuchh ṭhaṇḍā?
lines.en: What will you have — tea, or something cold?

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.native: कोई तकलीफ़ मत कीजिए, आंटी। बस पानी दे दीजिए।
lines.roman: koī taklīf mat kījiye, āṇṭī. bas pānī de dījiye.
lines.en: Please don't go to any trouble, aunty. Just water, please.

lines.speaker: Mrs Verma
lines.native: तकलीफ़ कैसी? आप हमारे मेहमान हैं। मैं चाय बनाऊँ?
lines.roman: taklīf kaisī? āp hamāre mehmān haiṃ. maiṃ chāy banāūṃ?
lines.en: What trouble? You're our guest. Shall I make some tea?

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.en: Alright, that's very kind of you.

lines.speaker: Mr Verma
lines.native: खाना तैयार है। चलिए, खाना खाएँ।
lines.roman: khānā taiyār hai. chaliye, khānā khāyeṃ.

lines.speaker: Mrs Verma
lines.native: और पनीर लीजिए। एक रोटी और?
lines.roman: aur panīr lījiye. ek roṭī aur?
lines.en: Have some more paneer. Another roti?

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.native: नहीं आंटी, बस। बहुत स्वादिष्ट था, पर पेट भर गया।
lines.roman: nahīṃ āṇṭī, bas. bahut svādiṣṭ thā, par peṭ bhar gayā.
lines.en: No aunty, that's enough. It was delicious, but I'm full.

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.native: अब मुझे इजाज़त दीजिए। बहुत देर हो गई।
lines.roman: ab mujhe ijāzat dījiye. bahut der ho gaī.
lines.en: Now, please allow me to leave. It's got very late.

lines.speaker: Mr Verma
lines.native: ज़रूर। फिर आइएगा! और घर पहुँचकर फ़ोन कीजिएगा।
lines.roman: zarūr. phir āiyegā! aur ghar pahuṃchkar fon kījiyegā.
lines.en: Of course. Do come again! And please call when you get home.

culture: Guests are treated almost as sacred — the Sanskrit saying *अतिथि देवो भव* means 'the guest is God'. Expect to be offered food and drink repeatedly; refusing once is seen as modesty, so say clearly but warmly **बस, पेट भर गया** if you mean it. Bring a small gift (sweets, fruit) when visiting a home. To leave, Hindi speakers don't just say 'bye' — they **ask permission**: **अब इजाज़त दीजिए** or **अब मैं चलता/चलती हूँ**, and hosts reply **फिर आइएगा** 'do come again'. Young people often greet elders by touching their feet (पैर छूना) and receive a blessing (आशीर्वाद) in return.

tip.title: दीजिए, दीजिएगा — the politeness ladder
tip.body:
- **दो** (friends) → **दीजिए** (polite) → **दे दीजिए** (smooth, 'for me') → **दीजिएगा** (extra courteous).
- Or ask: **क्या आप … देंगे?** / **… दे सकते हैं?** 'could you…?'
- **ज़रा** 'just' softens any request: **ज़रा** सुनिए.
- Extra polite: करना → **कीजिएगा**, जाना → **जाइएगा**.
tip.pattern: stem + इए / इएगा  ·  क्या आप … सकते हैं?

tip.title: मैं आऊँ? चलें? — shall I, shall we
tip.body:
- The subjunctive is the future **without -गा**: मैं करूँ, वह करे, हम / आप करें.
- **Shall I?** मैं चाय बनाऊँ? · **May I?** मैं अंदर आऊँ?
- **Shall we / let's**: चलें? · चलो, बाहर चलें.
- Also for wishes: आप ख़ुश रहें 'may you be happy'.

tip.title: अपना — my own, your own
tip.body:
- When the owner is the **subject**, use **अपना** instead of मेरा / उसका / आपका: मैं **अपना** काम करता हूँ 'I do my work'.
- It agrees like an -आ adjective: **अपना** (m), **अपनी** (f), **अपने** (pl, or before a postposition).
- **ख़ुद** = 'myself / yourself': मैं **ख़ुद** कर लूँगा.
